title: Class and unit group oracle corpus
objective: Integrate the deterministic class/unit oracle corpus into public acceptance tests and document proof semantics, provenance, capabilities, resource behavior, and benchmark policy

handoff.summary: Added a normalized degree 6 through 10 corpus for x^n-x-1 with exact signatures, discriminants, equation-order indices, class and unit invariants, regulators, and prime splitting through every exact Minkowski bound. A persistent timeout-safe harness obtains independent agreement from Sage/PARI, Magma, and Julia/Hecke and ignores timing drift in correctness comparisons. Installed Julia 1.10.10 in a task-scoped prefix, instantiated Hecke 0.40.0 and Oscar 1.9.0-DEV, and documented Oscar's Hecke 0.39 compatibility boundary. Focused class/unit test helpers now invoke bin/sagejs-source.cjs through process.execPath on native Windows instead of relying on extensionless or temporary cmd launchers.
risks: At e28e63bd a stale local FLINT addon makes the general D=12 public acceptance return incomplete with reason FLINT did not return exact outward dyadic endpoints. Root independently confirmed that an explicit FLINT rebuild passes the new endpoint tests; a separate build-cache lane owns that infrastructure fix. Specialized K.class_group() and K.unit_group() pass.
The independent algorithm=minkowski D=12 path returns incomplete with integer modulo by zero for its empty factor base; the engine lane owns the imminent fix.
Magma 2.18-5 Cputime is coarse and its retained one-sample timings are historical context, not gates.
The x^5-1009 unconditional Magma computation is metadata-only after an intentional 60-second interruption and is excluded from ordinary tiers.
next_steps: Run SAGEJS_SLOW_CLASS_UNIT=1 node --test test/number-field-class-unit-public.cjs on a dedicated host to record both quintic proof-mode timings without burdening ordinary CI.
Validate the process.execPath Windows launcher against the final integrated source after the engine and build-cache commits land.
Ratchet the directional warm thresholds only from uncontended five-sample Sage.js implementation measurements.
